summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis due to missed Novolog insulin, with concurrent acute on chronic pancreatitis. She presented with severe abdominal pain, nausea, and hyperglycemia. Initial management included IV fluids, insulin therapy, and pain control with IV Dilaudid. Her diet was advanced slowly after NPO status, though early self-advancement to solids delayed progress. A behavioral outburst led to GJ tube damage, which was replaced but with a clear warning against future breaks. Anxiety and aggression were managed with diazepam and the initiation of Celexa. Her condition improved over 17 days, with resolution of pancreatitis symptoms and stabilization of glucose. She was discharged home with updated insulin dosing, continued pain management, and a new outpatient care plan including psychiatric support.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
